samples.summary: `BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS` is a new, fourth hand-maintained enumeration of the boolean inline-style keys. The repo already enumerates the same set in `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:241, which is documented as "the single source of truth" for inline-style keysets in view/editor.ts:2738) and in the `KEYS` lists at view/editor.ts:2648 and view/text-box-editor.ts:1009. Putting the new list in `model/document.ts` rather than beside `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` in `model/types.ts` adds one more place to forget when a boolean inline key is added (Phase B of docs/design/slides/slides-font-ooxml-parity.md:179-181 plans exactly that, and its "every new field is added to …" checklist was not updated to mention this list).
samples.evidence: const BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS = ['bold','italic','underline','strikethrough','superscript','subscript'] as const; // vs CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE in model/types.ts:241

samples.summary: The new invariant is recorded only in `docs-font-controls.md`, a feature doc about the font toolbar, yet it is described in the text itself as a *storage* invariant spanning the docs model (`Doc.applyInlineStyle`), the store merge (`store/block-helpers.ts`), the slides text-box editor and the Yorkie CRDT. The canonical subsystem doc (docs/design/docs/docs.md) and the doc that owns the named-style cascade it depends on (docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md — the source of the Heading-6-italic exception) are not updated or cross-linked, so a reader of the model/named-styles docs will not learn the run-storage rule.
samples.evidence: ### Storage invariant: a boolean turned off is *cleared*, not stored as `false` … holds across the docs engine, the slides text-box editor … and the Yorkie store

samples.summary: The invariant is stated as a storage invariant but is enforced only at the top layer (`Doc.applyInlineStyle` / `applyInlineStyleToCells`). `DocStore.applyStyle` (memory store and YorkieDocStore) still happily stores an explicit `false`, so any writer that does not route through `Doc` — remote edits from an older peer, importers, tests, future callers of the exported `applyInlineStyleHelper` (packages/docs/src/index.ts:82) — reintroduces the dead flag. Enforcing at the merge (block-helpers) or in `inlineStylesEqual`/`normalizeInlines` would have made the invariant unbypassable at the layer that owns run storage.

No migration/normalization for `false` flags already persisted: documents written by earlier builds (and any peer still on an old build during the rollout) keep the dead flag, so the fragmentation and the named-style pinning that issue #749 reports persist in those documents until a user re-toggles the exact key. Nothing in `normalizeInlines`, `inlineStylesEqual`, `setDocument` or the Yorkie load path drops a `false`. The diff declares this out of scope in prose; if the issue's acceptance covers 'runs re-merge / style redefinition cascades' for existing documents, that criterion is unmet.
samples.evidence: Out of scope: `false` flags already stored by older builds are left alone — they resolve identically and are cleared the next time the user toggles that key.

samples.summary: The named-style exception hard-wires docs-specific cascade semantics into the shared model that slides also drives. `resolveStyleInline`/`BUILTIN_STYLES` (named-styles.ts:82-92) supplies a truthy boolean for exactly one key in one style (heading-6 italic), while the slides text box — which reuses this same `Doc` — resolves its typography from PPTX/theme data, not from docs' `BUILTIN_STYLES`. So in slides the exception branch can never fire correctly, and any slides-side default that does supply a boolean would be silently cleared instead of overridden.

Nothing in `normalizeInlines`, `inlineStylesEqual`, `setDocument` or the Yorkie load path drops a `false`. finding.evidence: Out of scope: `false` flags already stored by older builds are left alone — they resolve identically and are cleared the next time the user toggles that key.

verdict.reason: The absence is factually real — I confirmed no code drops a persisted `false`: `inlineStylesEqual` compares booleans strictly (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:404-424), `normalizeInlines`/`normalizeInlinesArray` only merge on that strict comparison (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:76-81; packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:905-912), `mergeInlineStyle` deletes only keys the current patch sets to `undefined` (block-helpers.ts:316-325), `styleOffAsClear` acts only on keys in the current write (document.ts:399-418), and the Yorkie load path faithfully rehydrates `bold: false` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:165-179). However it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric: the repo's spec surface for issue #749, docs/tasks/active/20260819-docs-inline-style-off-clears-key-todo.md:49-67, lists acceptance as exactly the three implemented items (demote `false` in Doc.applyInlineStyle/applyInlineStyleToCells, drop `undefined` keys in block-helpers.applyInlineStyle, tests incl. the named-style exception) and its Non-goals explicitly stop at the write path/model-level merge; migrating already-persisted flags is not an acceptance criterion or a breached Non-Goal. Design-doc discipline is met, not violated — the limitation is recorded in the canonical subsystem doc (docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:280-283). The finding is also self-hedged ("if the issue's acceptance covers…"), and that condition does not hold. Legacy-data remediation here is a follow-up wish, i.e. minor/non-blocking under this lens (and arguably a correctness-lens concern).
